memory: Confirmed: geometry creates centroid kink; lateral offsets relocate but leave residual ~0.0025 N·m at +0.60 mm. Neoprene attenuation: 0.25 mm→0.0016, 0.50 mm→0.0009, 0.75 mm→0.00065, 1.00 mm→0.00047 N·m. Diminishing returns are strong past 0.5 mm; values approach an asymptote near 0.00045 N·m. Tradeoff quantified: contact-band width increases (0.50→1.00 mm = +0.22 mm) and centroid uncertainty roughly doubles. Current position: attenuation below 0.0005 N·m is possible but costs measurable spatial and temporal fidelity. Next objective: determine if thicker spacers continue to lower tau_c meaningfully versus further eroding resolution.
openQuestion: If spacer thickness increases to 1.25 mm, will tau_c fall below 0.00045 N·m and how much will centroid uncertainty and imprint onset delay increase?
